trivia: Selected for preservation in the US Library of Congress National Recording Registry in 2012.
Widely considered by Deadheads and critics to be one of the greatest live performances in rock history.
Features a legendary 15-minute 'St. Stephen' -> 'Not Fade Away' -> 'St. Stephen' jam suite.
Jazz saxophonist Branford Marsalis sat in for the entire second set, creating a legendary 'Eyes of the World'.
Jerry Garcia praised Branford's playing, stating it felt like playing with an official member of the band.
Released as the acclaimed live album 'Without a Net' and 'Wake Up to Find Out'.
Benefit concert for the Springfield Creamery owned by Ken Kesey's family ('Sunshine Daydream').
The temperature on stage reached over 100°F during a legendary 31-minute performance of 'Dark Star'.
Filmed and released as the famous concert documentary movie 'Sunshine Daydream'.
The final concert ever held at the legendary Winterland Arena before its permanent closing.
Promoter Bill Graham descended from the ceiling in a giant glowing cannabis joint at midnight.
The band played a marathon 5-hour set lasting past 5:00 AM, serving breakfast to the audience at dawn.
Historic first performance where Jerry Garcia debuted his custom Doug Irwin 'Tiger' guitar on stage.
Part of the 'Day on the Green' festival lineup co-headlining with elements of Jefferson Starship.
The opening show of the massive 1987 Spring/Summer Tour following Jerry Garcia's health recovery.
Preceded the release of 'In the Dark', the album that launched 'Touch of Grey' into the Top 10.
The final concert ever performed at JFK Stadium before it was condemned and demolished.
Attended by over 74,000 Deadheads and released as the famous 'Crimson White & Indigo' concert film.
Famous late-night Friday the 13th show featuring acoustic and electric sets.
Duane Allman and Peter Green sat in during an epic late-night jam on 'Dark Star' -> 'Spanish Jam'.
Halloween night show during the 15th Anniversary Radio City Music Hall residency.
Opened by comedians Al Franken and Tom Davis, broadcast live via satellite to closed-circuit theaters.
Featured Bruce Hornsby on grand piano and accordion alongside Vince Welnick.
Part of an acclaimed 6-night sellout run at the historic Boston Garden.
